news.Title: Hyperscalers Bet on AI & Quantum: Watch GOOGL, AMZN, IBM in September
news.Content:
The AI buildout is no longer a future investment game. Hyperscalers are committing hundreds of billions of dollars to data centers, accelerators, networking and power infrastructure to meet surging demand for AI workloads. The scale is evident in Alphabet's planned $195-$205 billion of 2026 capital spending, while Google Cloud revenues jumped 82% year over year in the second quarter of 2026.

Quantum computing is following a different path. Governments and corporations are increasing funding as the technology moves closer to practical applications, but commercial revenues remain far smaller and the investment timeline considerably longer. The U.S. government recently committed $300 million under the CHIPS and Science Act to D-Wave Quantum QBTS, Rigetti Computing RGTI and Quantinuum, with each company receiving $100 million in R&D funding in exchange for minority government stakes. Yet D-Wave and Rigetti remained more than 25% below their 2026 starting levels even after the announcement.

This divergence matters for investors in the rest of September. Rather than chasing volatile pure-play quantum stocks, investors can gain exposure to the longer-term quantum opportunity through established technology companies that are already generating substantial AI and cloud revenue. IBM IBM, Alphabet GOOGL and Amazon AMZN offer three different ways to participate in this convergence while relying on businesses with current commercial demand to support the investment case.

AI Infrastructure Has a Longer Runway

The scale of the AI buildout supports this approach. PwC estimatesglobal data-center capital spending to reach $31.6 trillion through 2050, with annual spending rising from about $800 billion in 2026 to $1.8 trillion by 2050. The firm expects recurring server, GPU and other equipment upgrades to drive much of the long-term investment.

Per McKinsey, quantum-computing companies generated more than $1 billion of revenues in 2025, with potential to rise to $4.4 billion by 2028. More than 300 companies are already experimenting with quantum technology, but McKinsey also notes that the return on investment remains difficult to quantify because many applications are still experimental or hybrid.

This favors diversified technology leaders over pure-play quantum companies for the remainder of 2026.

3 Stocks to Watch in September

Alphabet: It offers a combination of hyperscaler economics, AI monetization and quantum optionality. Google Cloud revenues jumped 82% year over yearin the second quarter of 2026, while Cloud backlog reached $514 billion. Alphabet also raised its 2026 capital-spending guidance to $195-$205 billion, with AI infrastructure driving a significant portion of the investment.

Story Continues

Alphabet is also advancing its quantum-computing efforts. Google Quantum AI expanded its research into neutral-atom systems in 2026 and expects commercially relevant quantum computers to become available by the end of the decade. This gives GOOGL exposure to quantum computing without relying on near-term quantum revenues.

GOOGL is projected to report full-year 2026 earnings growth of 89.6% on revenue growth of 26%. The stock carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Amazon : Its AI-led development is increasingly centered on AWS, where growth is accelerating as customers expand AI workloads. AWS sales surged 37% year over year in the second quarter, its fastest growth in 18 quarters, pushing the business to a $169 billion annualized revenue run rate. Amazon also said its AI business surpassed a $25 billion annual revenue run rate, growing at a triple-digit rate.

Amazon is expanding its AI infrastructure ecosystem through custom chips and recently entered a long-term partnership with Qualcomm under which it could purchase up to $60 billion of AI data-center chips and related products. The companies are also developing custom silicon and optical connectivity solutions for AI data centers, with the initial focus on AI inference. AWS also operates Amazon Braket, giving customers cloud access to multiple quantum-computing architectures.

AMZN is projected to report full-year 2026 earnings growth of 82.2% on revenue growth of 15.7%. The stock carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy).

IBM: It provides the strongest direct quantum exposure among the three while retaining a substantial enterprise AI and hybrid-cloud business. In the second quarter of 2026, software revenues increased 5% with Hybrid Cloud (Red Hat) revenues up 11% and Data revenues up 19%. IBM expects 2026 constant-currency revenue growth of 4%-5% and plans to invest more than $10 billion in quantum over the next five years.

IBM's quantum roadmap targets quantum advantage in 2026 and a large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computer by 2029. The company also announced a quantum innovation hub with Lockheed Martin in Switzerland this week, with an IBM Quantum System Two to be deployed at the Swiss National Supercomputing Centre. The initiative expands IBM's quantum ecosystem across research, government and industrial applications.

IBM is projected to report full-year 2026 earnings growth of 6.4% on revenue growth of 4.3%. The stock carries a Zacks Rank #3. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

news.Title: NVIDIA vs. AMD After Earnings: Which AI Stock Should You Buy Now?
news.Content:
NVIDIA Corporation NVDA and Advanced Micro Devices, Inc . AMD have both gained immensely from soaring demand for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure and recently posted strong quarterly results. However, NVIDIA remains the market leader, while AMD continues to gain ground. So, which AI stock offers the better investment opportunity right now? Let's see in detail –

NVIDIA's AI Growth Surges as Data Center Demand Rises

NVIDIA's Data Center business has remained the primary growth engine. Data Center revenues were $89 billion in the fiscal second quarter of 2027, up 117% year over year and 18% quarter over quarter, according to the company's Aug. 26 press release. Overall, NVIDIA generated $96.2 billion in revenues, up 106% year over year and 18% sequentially.

Alongside rapid revenue growth, NVIDIA exhibited strong profitability. During the quarter, NVIDIA's GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins both came in at 75% compared with roughly 72.5% a year ago. The company is also translating rapid revenue growth into even faster earnings growth, supported by continued gains in operating income.

NVIDIA now projects revenues of around $108 billion, plus or minus 2%, for the fiscal third quarter of 2027, up 12% sequentially from the midpoint. Thus, NVIDIA's growth trajectory remains robust, while its cutting-edge Vera Rubin platform is in full production, indicating that the company is well-poised to gain from the next phase of AI infrastructure spending.

AMD's Strong Data Center Growth Bolsters Its AI Ambitions

The Data Center segment was the primary driver of AMD's revenue growth, with sales doubling from the same period a year ago in the second quarter of 2026, according to the company's Aug. 4 press release. Total revenues reached $11.5 billion, up 50% year over year and 13% from the previous quarter.

Strong demand for AMD's EPYC server processors boosted revenue growth. At the same time, the company's Helios platform has entered its initial ramp-up phase, while its Instinct accelerators continue to scale rapidly. Consequently, AMD projects third-quarter 2026 revenues to reach $13 billion, plus or minus $300 million. At the midpoint, this would represent 41% year-over-year growth and a 13% sequential increase.

AMD also expects Data Center revenues to improve further in the latter half of 2026, and profitability is projected to improve steadily. The company projects a 56% non-GAAP gross margin in the third quarter, indicating continued progress in margin expansion.

NVIDIA vs. AMD: Why NVDA Is the Stronger AI Stock to Buy Now

Story Continues

The rollout of NVIDIA's advanced Vera Rubin platform, strong margins, and sheer dominance in AI infrastructure, driven largely by Data Center growth, are expected to support a positive movement in its shares. AMD, meanwhile, is closing the gap through strong Data Center growth, expanding AI accelerator sales, and improving profitability.

Despite AMD's growing momentum with its EPYC server processors and Instinct accelerators, NVIDIA's full-stack platform gives the company a competitive edge as AI infrastructure spending increases. With a larger AI infrastructure footprint, NVIDIA remains the market leader.

Moreover, NVIDIA's net profit margin of 63.7% versus AMD's 15.6% highlights NVIDIA's greater efficiency in converting revenues into bottom-line earnings. Therefore, NVIDIA remains the stronger buy, backed by superior profitability, AI infrastructure leadership and full-stack platform advantage.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Additionally, NVIDIA appears more attractively valued than AMD. By price-to-earnings ratio, NVDA trades at 24.26 forward earnings compared with AMD's 69.59 forward earnings multiple.

NVIDIA currently has a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), while AMD has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 stocks here.

O'Connor opines that about 45% of Intel's current market capitalization assumes that the company's foundry unit will gain a whopping 15 points of market share in CPUs globally. That's possible -- but far from guaranteed. Should Intel's gains prove more muted than that, much of the last year's gains could evaporate.

news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Alphabet Inc. ( GOOGL , Financials ), the parent company of Google and one of the largest cloud and AI providers , is taking its infrastructure deeper into university research.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 2 Warning Signs with YB.

Is GOOGL fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Google Public Sector is partnering with Morgan State University to build an AI-focused research campus supporting work in cybersecurity, climate science, health science and large language models.

The project will give researchers access to high-end GPU computing through Google Cloud and Nvidia infrastructure.

That is the obvious part. The longer-term opportunity is what happens after students and researchers become comfortable building on Google's technology.

Morgan State also plans to create a Google-focused Center of Excellence for AI skills and workforce training. Faculty will gain access to Google for Startups, while the university will use Google SecOps and Mandiant security tools for research requiring stricter controls.

The partnership also connects Google to Morgan State's Obsidian AI platform, including projects involving traffic and urban mobility in Baltimore. For Alphabet, these deals are small compared with multibillion-dollar cloud contracts.

But they can still matter. Training future engineers and researchers on Google Cloud can make the platform harder to replace later.

For investors, the question is whether partnerships like this can quietly translate into greater cloud adoption as universities, startups and public-sector organizations expand their AI spending.

news.Title: Advanced Micro Devices vs. Nvidia: Which Semiconductor Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
news.Content:
As the artificial intelligence revolution matures, investors are weighing the long-term potential of Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) against the market dominance of Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) to see which chipmaker offers more value.

AMD operates as a flexible challenger, providing essential chips for data centers and gaming consoles while expanding its presence in the AI accelerator market. Nvidia remains the industry titan, leveraging a comprehensive platform of hardware and software to dominate the accelerated computing landscape. Both companies are critical to the modern digital economy, but they offer different risk profiles.

The case for Advanced Micro Devices

Advanced Micro Devices designs high-performance computing products ranging from data center processors to gaming consoles. Among semiconductor stocks , its MI450 GPU deal with OpenAI and chips for Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) highlight its growing AI presence. Relying on a small number of large customers for a majority of sales adds a layer of risk to the business.

In the fiscal year ended Dec. 27, 2025, according to its latest annual report, revenue reached nearly $34.6 billion. This represented growth of approximately 34.3% compared with the prior fiscal year. Net income was roughly $4.3 billion, yielding a net margin of close to 12.5%, a significant improvement over the prior year's net margin of about 6.4%.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.1x, indicating the company maintains a conservative level of borrowing. The current ratio is roughly 2.9x, while free cash flow, which is cash from operations minus capital expenditures, reached nearly $5.5 billion. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 21.2% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

The case for Nvidia

Nvidia provides the accelerated computing platforms that underpin the current boom in artificial intelligence. Its data center infrastructure and software are used by major cloud service providers and AI model developers to host advanced applications. The company also maintains a strong presence in the automotive industry through its DRIVE platform, which supports hundreds of partners including various OEMs.

According to its latest annual report, in the fiscal year ended Jan. 25, 2026, revenue reached approximately $215.9 billion. This represents a 65.5% increase year over year, driven by intense demand for AI chips. Net income for the period was roughly $120.1 billion, resulting in a net margin of close to 55.6%.

Story Continues

As of the January 2026 balance sheet, Nvidia reported a debt-to-equity ratio of nearly 0.1x. The current ratio is roughly 3.9x, while free cash flow for the fiscal year ended Jan. 25, 2026, was approximately $96.7 billion. This massive cash generation provides the company with significant flexibility to reinvest in research or return capital to shareholders.

Risk profile comparison

AMD faces intense competition from Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) and Nvidia, including a recent partnership between those two rivals that could pressure its market share. The company relies heavily on TSMC for manufacturing, while geopolitical tensions and U.S. export controls on advanced chips to China have led to inventory charges. Ongoing litigation regarding securities laws also poses a potential financial and regulatory hurdle.

Nvidia is also vulnerable to tightening U.S. export controls, which have already restricted its data center sales in China. Competition is evolving as major cloud customers like Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN), Microsoft, and Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) develop their own AI chips in-house. Additionally, antitrust regulators in several jurisdictions are scrutinizing its sales practices and market dominance.

Valuation comparison

Nvidia appears significantly cheaper than its rival based on its Forward P/E , which uses future earnings estimates, though its P/S ratio remains slightly higher.

Which stock would I buy in 2026?

I'd go with Nvidia, and it's not a close call. Nvidia just posted one of the most extraordinary quarters in the history of the semiconductor industry. Revenue more than doubled year over year, data center demand is accelerating rather than plateauing, and the company guided for another massive jump in the quarter ahead. Jensen Huang's observation that AI has reached its inflection point (that its tokens are now productive and profitable) captures why the demand behind these numbers is not a temporary surge.

AMD deserves credit for its own impressive run. Data center sales more than doubled year over year, an Anthropic partnership adds long-term credibility, and AMD is cementing its position as the primary alternative to Nvidia in the AI chip market. For a long-term investor who wants AI chip exposure at a lower price point, AMD is a reasonable choice.

But "the primary alternative to Nvidia" is a very different position than being Nvidia. The gap in scale, ecosystem depth, and customer lock-in between these two companies is enormous and widening. For a long-term investor, owning the company that the entire AI industry is built around is a stronger foundation than owning its closest competitor.

群益台灣精選高息（00919）ETF經理人謝明志強調，市場上每檔台股高息ETF的成分股篩選機制都不同，各有千秋，投資人一定不希望領高股息賠價差，後續來看，台股雖然多頭格局未變，但切忌追高，應採分批布局策略，金控股擁有獲利具爆發力、獲利具續航力、現金股利率大幅優於市場平均，為高股息ETF必選成分股、股價漲幅跟不上獲利成長等四大利基，因此，建議投資人可續抱金融持股比例高的台股高股息ETF。

主動群益核心50（00415A）ETF經理人許育誌表示，近期大盤呈現防禦性輪動，資金自高估值AI權值股流出，轉進低基期次族群與金融板塊。不過AI供應鏈基本面未變，只是從過去全面齊漲，轉為「輪動加速、個股分化」，也更加彰顯主動選股、汰弱留強的重要性。基於全球AI投資與需求仍相當強勁，台廠可望同步受惠，尤其在記憶體、封測、晶圓材料、ABF、PCB/CCL、光通訊、半導體廠務工程等領域台廠於全球供應鏈中扮演領頭角色，相關個股表現仍值期待。（自立電子報2026/9/10）

news.Title: 美國PPI出爐「台股夜盤又崩了」！專家籲短線逢高快減碼：9月很可能有低買機會
news.Content:
美國公布8月PPI最新統計數據，美股期指走低，台股夜盤也跟著大跌逾800點。示意圖。（資料照，陳品佑攝）

美國公布最新統計數據，8月生產者物價指數（PPI）月增0.4%、與去年同期相比增5.4%，略高於市場預期；核心PPI則是年增4.6%，符合預期表現。不過數據公布後，美股期指走低，台股夜盤也跟著大跌逾800點，對此，財經作家狄驤指出，雖然短線上有不少變數，但他「逢高持續減碼」的策略仍沒有變，且9月往往會有更好的低買機會出現。

狄驤表示，美國8月PPI略高於預期，核心PPI表現不錯，但台股夜盤仍跌，近3個交易日已經跌掉1000點。畢竟國際油價一直飆，市場的通膨預期短線上壓不下來，跟他早上提到川普的說辭可能也有關，這就是他早上分享會保守減碼的原因之一。

狄驤指出，不過，市場本來就預期PPI升溫與CPI持平，意味著企業不會大幅轉嫁成本給消費者，「所以我是樂觀看待明天的CPI」；然而假如國際油價續漲，CPI符合預期的正面影響，就會被快速消化，所以重點仍要看國際油價何時跌回100美元以下。

短線變數多　台股該如何操作？

狄驤分析，雖然短線上有不少變數，但他的整體規劃沒有改變，近期就是「逢高持續減碼」，歷年9月往往會有更好的低買機會，今年再加上各種總經變化後，相似的歷史有望重演，所以他們才會先行應對，未雨綢繆。

狄驤強調，老話一句，「逢高獲利減碼，總比獲利快速縮水才緊張殺低來得好。」講起來很簡單，但實際上他們一直在綜合判斷市場風險，所謂的「逢高減碼」，其實更偏向於「風險高時才減碼」。

news.Title: Nvidia Is Suddenly Outpacing the S&P 500. Expect That to Continue.
news.Content:

Investors should expect Nvidia to continue beating the S&P 500, as it has done for many years. Strong financial results and the continuation of the artificial intelligence supercycle are two major reasons why.

Revenue growth continues to accelerate

It's very hard to find a company that generates substantial revenue and can still deliver accelerating growth rates. The company earned $96.2 billion in its fiscal 2027 second quarter, representing a 106% year-over-year growth rate. Based on guidance , the chipmaker will soon bring in more than $100 billion per quarter.

All of those earnings also come with impressive margins. Net income more than doubled year over year, reaching $59.7 billion in the process. Nvidia has consistently shown that the AI supercycle is gaining momentum. People have called it a bubble for a while, but with Nvidia anticipating 70% year-over-year revenue growth in its fiscal 2028, the bubble concerns have become quiet murmurs.

Even the company's valuation is solid. It trades at a 25.4 forward P/E ratio and has a PEG ratio below 0.60. Nvidia's fundamentals are improving at a faster rate than its stock price, suggesting its valuation could become even more attractive when it reports earnings again later in the year.

Nvidia is the clear leader

Nvidia earns higher quarterly profits than most chipmakers generate in quarterly revenue. That gives investors an idea of how much market share Nvidia has over the competition, and as the AI boom accelerates, Nvidia is well-positioned to increase its lead.

Its Vera Rubin platform is about to show up in future results, and it's not just hyperscalers driving the demand.

"This time last year, one lab alone was driving the buildout; today, we have a golden age of new AI labs and start-ups, multiple frontier labs scaling in parallel," Jensen Huang said in the Q2 FY27 press release.

Huang also touted the arrival of physical AI when describing Nvidia's opportunity. While it's not an exclusive opportunity for Nvidia, the AI chipmaker is better positioned than any other company. Its GPUs are the technological bedrock, regardless of which companies figure out physical AI the fastest.

Story Continues

Nvidia's position, strengthening fundamentals, and reasonable valuation make it an easy pick that could outperform the S&P 500 over an extended period. Nvidia's sluggish start was a fluke that investors have rightly called out, as evidenced by the recent accumulation.

news.Title: This Market Indicator Is Sending a Warning Signal to Investors. Here's What History Says the S&P 500 Does Next.
news.Content:
Although there's been some pullbacks along the way, the stock market has gone up and to the right since the start of 2023.

This year, the broader benchmark S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) is up more than 12% (as of Sept. 9), and that's despite some pretty significant challenges, including the Iran war, which has led oil prices to soar. It also includes trade wars, elevated inflation, a potential interest rate hike, and concerns about artificial intelligence (AI).

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

However, continued earnings growth, largely on the back of the AI infrastructure build-out, has helped the S&P 500 overcome these potential drags and deliver solid performance overall.

But that doesn't mean there aren't still worries. In fact, one market indicator in particular is sending a clear warning signal to investors. Here's what history says the S&P 500 Index will do next.

The Shiller CAPE Ratio is sending the market an obvious warning sign

Investors use many data points and metrics, whether it's to track individual stocks or a broader benchmark. One for the S&P 500 specifically is the Shiller CAPE ratio , which compares the S&P 500's value to its inflation-adjusted 10-year average earnings.

The concept is somewhat similar to a price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio, but the Shiller CAPE adjusts for inflation and uses a 10-year average to smooth out irregularities that will inevitably occur across a business cycle.

For instance, in some years there might be strong gross domestic product (GDP) growth, while in others there might be weak growth. There can also be erratic events that affect the entire market and economy, such as the COVID-19 pandemic, which then led to the highest inflation in 40 years in 2022.

The point being, you never want to rely on just one year's earnings to tell an entire story.

S&P 500 Shiller CAPE Ratio data by YCharts

As shown above, the Shiller CAPE ratio is now more than 40, well above its long-term average, and not too far from levels seen in 2000, right before the dot-com bubble burst, which led to a major sell-off.

Here's what happens next, according to history

Investors have frequently cited similarities between the current AI revolution and the internet bubble of 2000. Both were driven by game-changing technologies that would go on to disrupt society as we know it.

Story Continues

Both cycles also involve spending exorbitant amounts of money to build the infrastructure that powers these technologies. When the dot-com bubble burst in 2000, here's what happened to the S&P 500 and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite during the next few years.

^SPX data by YCharts

Many internet start-ups went bankrupt, while even large, established tech companies saw their stocks get crushed.

Now, as most know, stocks would eventually recover, but it didn't happen overnight. In fact, it took the Nasdaq 15 years to return to its previous high levels right before the dot-com bubble burst.

So, if history repeats, the S&P 500 has a little more room to move higher before a severe pullback, which it would then regain over time. However, it's also important for investors to note that while history often rhymes, it rarely repeats.

A negative for the S&P 500 is that it is more heavily concentrated in AI companies today than it was during the dot-com era.

Today, the 10 largest companies in the S&P 500, most of which are AI companies, make up roughly 40% of the index. In the dot-com era, the top 10 made up only 25%, according to UBS .

So if the AI bubble bursts, the S&P 500 could take a bigger hit today. However, I also think it's worth noting that everything seems to move much more quickly today, perhaps because of the internet and the degree to which trading has become digitized.

Even during these past three years, the market has experienced some severe sell-offs due to the Silicon Valley Bank crash in 2023, President Donald Trump's major tariff announcement in April 2025, and the Iran war this year.

All this is to say that nobody knows for sure what will happen.

Similar to the dot-com bubble, I do think the S&P 500 will experience a severe sell-off, likely driven by some issue with AI. Similar to the dot-com bust, I fully expect the market to recover and for AI to continue to fundamentally reshape the world.

news.Title: Applied Materials Eyes Nearly 40% Growth as AI Fuels Chip Equipment Demand
news.Content:
These 3 GARP Stocks Show Why Growth and Value Do Not Have to Clash

Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT) CEO Gary Dickerson said demand tied to artificial intelligence and data-center computing is strengthening the company's near-term and long-term outlook, with the semiconductor equipment maker now approaching 40% revenue growth for 2026 based on its recent communications.

Speaking at the Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference, Dickerson said Applied had raised its 2026 revenue-growth outlook several times during the year. The company initially projected growth of more than 20% in February, increased that view to more than 30% in May, and has since moved toward 40% growth, he said.

AI Drives Equipment Demand

→ 3 Under-the-Radar Defense Stocks With Record Backlogs

Applied Materials Beat Everything but Wall Street's Expectations for Margins

Dickerson characterized AI, particularly data-center AI, as the largest demand driver for Applied's business. He said leading-edge foundry logic, DRAM including high-bandwidth memory, and advanced packaging account for 80% of wafer fab equipment growth this year. Applied expects a similar mix in 2027 and beyond, he added.

He pointed to a shift in semiconductor demand between smartphones and data centers. Smartphone wafer starts at leading-edge foundries were four times larger than data-center wafer starts several years ago, according to Dickerson. He said the markets are now approximately equal, and data-center wafer starts could become twice as large as smartphone wafer starts within a few years.

→ Ride-Share Reckoning: Tesla Drives Into Uber's Lane

MarketBeat Week in Review – 06/22 - 06/26

Applied has a rolling eight-quarter customer forecast as well as longer-term commitments, Dickerson said, adding that the company is holding discussions with customers extending through 2030. He said agentic AI is increasing expected demand for CPUs and DRAM, while physical AI could add further computing demand over time.

"AI is the biggest technology inflection I've ever seen in my life," Dickerson said, describing the trend as a multiyear driver rather than a typical semiconductor cycle.

Services and Internal AI Adoption

→ High Gas Prices Aren't Budging—Here Are 3 Stocks That Benefit

Dickerson said Applied is using AI primarily to accelerate product development and expand revenue opportunities, rather than focusing solely on cost reduction. He cited a 50% productivity improvement in software and algorithm development for certain products, saying the aim is to bring multibillion-dollar products to market more quickly.

Story Continues

The company also is applying AI to its services business, where Dickerson said demand for yield and output improvements has increased. Applied has more than 37,000 chambers in the field connected to AI-enabled servers, most of them remotely connected, he said. The company is using predictive models, preventive maintenance and chamber-matching capabilities to help customers increase output and improve the number of good chips produced per wafer.

Applied's services business grew more than 20% year over year, Dickerson said, while service margins improved by 180 basis points. In some cases, he said, new service contracts can more than double revenue per tool.

Advanced Packaging and Process Control Growth

Advanced packaging is expected to be one of Applied's fastest-growing businesses. Dickerson said the segment is forecast to grow more than 70% this year and is expected to generate between $2 billion and $3 billion in revenue at the midpoint of the company's forecast range.

High-bandwidth memory and 3D integrated circuits are among the fastest-growing advanced-packaging areas, he said. Applied has added capabilities through acquisitions in panel-level plating and X-ray technology, according to Dickerson.

Applied's inspection and measurement business, meanwhile, is growing more than 50% in the current calendar year, he said. Dickerson highlighted the company's electron-beam and optical technologies, which he said support both chip performance improvements and yield gains.

Semiconductor Systems gross margin has increased by about 190 basis points over the past year to the mid-50% range, Dickerson said.

Service margins increased 180 basis points over the same period.

Dickerson said he expects Applied to continue expanding margins because of the value its technologies provide in performance, yield and output.

Regional Outlook and Capital Allocation

In China, Applied is primarily exposed to its ICAPS markets, which include internet-of-things, communications, automotive, power, sensors and consumer electronics. Dickerson said the company is seeing growth in China and gaining some share in areas where it can compete, but expects ICAPS to grow at mid- to high-single-digit rates over time, slower than AI data-center-related markets.

He said regionalization of semiconductor manufacturing is a tailwind for Applied's service business because newer manufacturing locations often have less-established service infrastructure and less experience ramping production yields.

Dickerson declined to discuss specific customers, including the proposed Terafab effort discussed by conference host Jim Schneider. He said Applied is engaged with companies pursuing AI-compute leadership and is working with customers on technology road maps spanning advanced logic, memory and packaging.

Looking ahead, Dickerson said 2027 should be "a great year" for Applied and that growth should remain strong beyond that period, though he did not provide a numerical forecast. On capital allocation, he said Applied expects to return 80% to 100% of cash to shareholders. Large acquisitions are difficult in the current geopolitical environment, he said, but the company will continue to pursue smaller acquisitions and strategic investments.

About Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT)

Applied Materials, Inc is a global provider of materials engineering solutions used to manufacture semiconductors, displays and other advanced electronic products. The company develops and supplies equipment, services and software that help customers build and improve the performance of chips and display panels.

Its semiconductor products support processes including deposition, etch, patterning, inspection, metrology and materials modification. Applied Materials also provides equipment and services for display manufacturing, including technologies used in producing liquid-crystal and organic light-emitting diode displays, as well as solutions for adjacent markets such as solar and other specialty applications.

Founded in 1967 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California, Applied Materials serves semiconductor and display manufacturers worldwide through operations, customer-support centers and research and development activities across major technology-producing regions.

news.Title: Understanding Disclosure Documents
news.Content:
Disclosure documents are written materials that provide important information about investments, firms and financial professionals. These documents can give you information when you're considering a new firm, opening a new account, trying a new investment strategy, or buying investment products such as stocks, bonds, mutual funds, exchange-traded funds (ETFs) or municipal securities. They also provide details of your transactions and holdings, as well as the fees and costs you pay.

According to the Investor Survey component of the FINRA Investor Education Foundation's 2024 National Financial Capability Study (NFCS), only 51 percent of investors recall receiving disclosures, and even fewer say they at least skim them. However, taking time to review disclosure documents can help you make better decisions, avoid surprises and spot potential problems early.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Here are some of the most common disclosure documents and information sources you might see when you invest:

Choosing a Firm or Investment Professional

Relationship Summary ( Form CRS ) – Broker-dealers and investment advisors are required to provide you with a relationship summary. This form tells you about the types of services the firm offers and the fees, costs, conflicts of interest, and required standards of conduct associated with those services. It also tells you whether the firm and its investment professionals have reportable legal or disciplinary history and how to get more information about the firm. Form CRS also includes key questions to ask your investment professional.

BrokerCheck – FINRA's free BrokerCheck tool can help you research the background and experience of investment professionals and firms. You can find information about employment history, qualifications, disciplinary history and more.

Regulation Best Interest ( Reg BI ) Disclosure – This document provides facts about your brokerage relationship, including services, products offered, fees and costs, and conflicts of interest.

Opening an Account

Account Agreement – This contract between you and your brokerage firm outlines how orders are executed, how disputes are resolved, account features and more. It also contains information about your legal rights and what authority the firm has to act on your behalf.

Privacy Notice – Known as a Regulation S-P notice, this disclosure details the types of information the firm collects, how it might be shared with affiliates or third parties, and what measures the firm takes to protect your data. This notice--which you receive at account opening and then once a year--also mentions your rights to opt out of information sharing.

Account-Specific Disclosures – Before approving you to engage in trading strategies using leverage--like options trading and margin --your brokerage firm is required to provide you with disclosures explaining the risks and costs. For example, the Characteristics and Risks of Standardized Options explains what options are, how they work and are priced, options strategies, risks involved in options trading, and the rules and procedures for exercising options and settling transactions. Other account-specific disclosures might provide fee schedules, specific account features or additional information.

Story Continues

Making Investments

Prospectus – A prospectus is a legal document that provides detailed information about registered securities offerings such as a stock, corporate bond, mutual fund, ETF or variable annuity. It explains the essential terms of the investment. The specific content of any prospectus varies depending on the type of security. Mutual funds and ETFs also typically have a summary prospectus--a shorter, more readable version that highlights the most important information, including investment objectives, fees, risks and past performance.

Official Statement – An official statement is a document prepared by or on behalf of a state or local government in connection with a new issue of municipal securities that describes the essential terms of the bonds. An official statement is similar to a prospectus for a corporate stock or bond offering.

Other Product-Specific Disclosures – Some investment products might have additional disclosures beyond offering documents. For example, certain alternative investments might have limited partnership agreements.

Staying Informed

Shareholder Reports – Funds disclose their holdings at least quarterly and also provide annual and semiannual reports to shareholders that highlight key information for assessing and monitoring your fund investments. Public companies file periodic reports that contain financial statements, management discussion and analysis, and material changes or risks related to their operations.

Updated Product Disclosures – Some investment product disclosures are updated regularly. Prospectuses for mutual funds and ETFs, for example, must be updated at least annually, as well as when there are material changes, such as a new manager or a change in strategy or fees.

Keeping Track of Your Accounts and Transactions

Your account statements and trade confirmations are among the most important disclosures you'll receive, because they reflect your specific holdings, transactions and costs. Reviewing them carefully and regularly is one of the most effective ways to stay on top of your investments and catch errors or potential misconduct early. If you find an inaccuracy or something you don't recognize, contact your firm right away. If the issue isn't resolved to your satisfaction, you can file a complaint with FINRA's online Complaint Center .

Account Statements – Brokerage firms and mutual fund companies must provide you with an account statement at least quarterly for accounts with any holdings. This statement lists all your positions, values, transactions and fees paid. Many firms voluntarily provide monthly statements to all customers.

Trade Confirmations – These list a price, fee and settlement date for each transaction you make. This information is crucial for verifying that your trades were executed as expected and that you're aware of the costs involved.

You can receive a disclosure via email, physical mail or your online account portal. Many required filings are also available from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission's (SEC's) EDGAR database , while those related to municipal securities are available from EMMA .

Disclosure documents exist to inform and protect you. When something's unclear, ask questions, especially before making any investment decisions, and stay alert to red flags that could indicate possible fraud, such as mentions of guaranteed returns or statements downplaying risk.

news.Title: 3 Quantum Stocks Just Scored $100 Million in Government Funding. Which Is the Best to Buy Now?
news.Content:
The race to develop a fault-tolerant quantum computer has been ongoing, and the stakes are high. The technology is expected to be the next big advancement after artificial intelligence, and the U.S. government wants to make sure that a U.S.-based company is leading the way. As such, the government recently doled out $100 million each to three quantum stocks under the CHIPS Act.

Which stock is the best buy will largely be determined by their technology and how far along each is. Let's dig into the three stocks to see which one stands out.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

1. Rigetti Computing

One of the companies getting $100 million in government funding is Rigetti Computing (NASDAQ: RGTI). As part of the deal, the U.S. government will also take a stake in the company.

The money will be used to help accelerate superconducting quantum research and improve current technical bottlenecks. The company specifically laid out three projects it will help fund. They include shrinking chip control electronics, massively expanding super-cooling freezer capacity, and manufacturing higher-density quantum chips.

The strength of the superconducting technology that Rigetti employs has always been speed. Its systems are about 10,000 times faster than trapped-ion systems and 100 times faster than neutral-atom systems. Where they struggle, though, is with accuracy, which is one of the most important hurdles that quantum computers need to overcome. While companies like IonQ have achieved 99.99% two- qubit gate fidelity (accuracy), Rigetti greatly trails with its Cepheus 1-108Q systems only hitting 99.1% two-gate fidelity.

2. D-Wave Quantum

Another company getting $100 million in U.S. government funding in exchange for giving the government an equity stake is D-Wave Quantum (NASDAQ: QBTS). The company will use the money to help develop and scale its annealing and gate-model quantum systems.

D-Wave is the leader in quantum annealing, which is a more narrow-purpose technology that helps solve optimization problems. The technology is much further along than more wide-ranging gate-based systems, and the company is already selling its Advantage II systems to commercial customers in industries such as logistics, finance, and defense.

At the same time, D-Wave has also started to pursue a gate-based system following its acquisition of Quantum Circuits earlier this year, which gave it a dual-rail gate-model processor with built-in error detection. For its systems, it will use fluxonium qubits, which are a type of superconducting qubit that has similar properties to those it uses for its annealing technology. D-Wave's goal is to create a system with the speed of superconducting and the accuracy of trapped ions, but it is still very early in the process.

Story Continues

3. Quantinuum

A third company getting a $100 million check from the government is Quantinuum (NASDAQ: QNT), although it did not have to give up an equity stake.

Quantunuum will use the proceeds to work with GlobalFoundries and Monarch Quantum to improve its supply chain. GlobalFoundries will be one of several foundries to produce its next-generation ion traps using 300mm wafer technology, while Monarch will develop and manufacture lasers and optical components for Quantunuum's trapped-ion systems.

The trapped-ion approach, while slower, has proven to be the most accurate quantum technology to-date. Quantunuum has achieved 99.92% two-qubit gate fidelity and is looking to reach 99.999% logical fidelity with its new Sol system next year.

Meanwhile, the company is considered to have one of the best software stacks in the space. This includes its open-source quantum computing language Guppy that does advanced error correction directly in the code and its TKET quantum software development kit that acts as a universal translator.

The verdict

The quantum computing race is far from over, and which technology eventually comes out on top is still up in the air. That said, I'd be betting on accuracy over speed at this point, which is why I prefer Quantinuum. The company is an accuracy leader and already starting to see meaningful revenue growth. Backed by industrial giant Honeywell, Quantunuum's stock has a lot of potential.

news.Title: 2 Trillion-Dollar Companies Poised to Become Wall Street's Next Stock-Split Stocks
news.Content:
Although artificial intelligence (AI) has been the hottest thing since sliced bread over the last four years, don't overlook the role stock-split euphoria has played in lifting the broader market. Companies undertaking forward stock splits , designed to lower their share price to make it more nominally affordable for retail investors, have effectively been magnets for everyday investors.

Two of Wall Street's elite trillion-dollar companies are ideally positioned to become Wall Street's next stock-split stocks . The only question is: Will the boards at social media titan Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) and memory juggernaut Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) take the leap?

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Meta Platforms can make "Magnificent Seven" history with a stock split

Mark Zuckerberg's company is unique in that it's the only "Magnificent Seven" member that's never completed a stock split. While fractional-share investing has become more common at online brokers and lessened the need for stock splits, it's fair to question if Meta's nearly $617 share price is keeping some retail investors from participating in its growth story.

Additionally, almost 30% of the company's outstanding shares are held by retail investors. Since institutional investors don't require a lower nominal share price, the higher the non-institutional ownership figure, the more of an impetus there is to conduct a forward split.

Beyond its high share price and sizable retail investor ownership, Meta's stock is well-positioned to rise over the long term. The company's family of apps, including Facebook, WhatsApp, Instagram, and Threads, attracted 3.6 billion daily active users in June. With no other social media platforms coming close to the figure, Meta is a prime destination for advertisers.

Meta Platforms has also successfully integrated AI solutions into its ad platforms. Giving clients access to generative AI enables them to tailor static and video messages to individual users. If this improves click-through rates, it only enhances the company's premium ad pricing power.

Micron hasn't split in more than a quarter-century

From a nominal dollar standpoint, Micron is even more likely to announce a stock split than Meta. It closed out the Labor Day weekend at nearly $1,017 per share, with everyday investors holding more than 26% of its outstanding shares. This is certainly a large enough retail investor presence to merit action by the board of directors, which hasn't approved a stock split since 2000.

Story Continues

But the primary stock-split catalyst is the belief that its share price will head even higher. Micron's claim to fame, and the reason its shares have rallied more than 1,100% over the trailing 16 months, is its ideal positioning as an AI-accelerated data center memory provider.

Micron's high-bandwidth memory (HBM) is packaged with graphics processing units, enabling lightning-fast data transfer speeds, which is necessary when software and systems are being tasked with split-second decision-making.

Furthermore, the insatiable demand for HBM solutions far outstrips supply, leading to both incredible pricing power for Micron and a backlog that's been booked more than a year in advance. The commoditization of memory and storage solutions often upends these companies after a short period. However, fully booked contracts through 2027 suggest that Micron's otherworldly sales and profit growth can continue for the foreseeable future.

news.Title: This Unstoppable Warren Buffett ETF Would Have Quadupled Your Money Over the Last Decade
news.Content:
Warren Buffett doesn't usually recommend his investments outright to others. He often praises some of his favorite stocks, like Coca-Cola and Apple , and he gives general investing advice, like avoiding overvalued stocks and looking at businesses rather than stock prices.

However, he has recommended investing in an S&P 500 index fund many times, and over the past 10 years, doing so would have quadrupled your money.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The easy way to grow your money

In 2013, Buffett described how he and Charlie Munger, his longtime business partner, spent their days analyzing businesses. However, he believes that the retail investor doesn't need to do that and can rely on the growth of the U.S. economy. "The goal of the non-professional should not be to pick winners...but should rather be to own a cross-section of businesses that in aggregate are bound to do well. A low-cost S&P 500 index fund will achieve this goal." He went on to recommend the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (NYSEMKT: VOO).

There's a lot packed into his statement. An S&P 500 exchange-traded fund provides an instant, diversified portfolio of stocks that are expected to grow over time. The Vanguard ETF, in particular, has a low expense ratio of only 0.03%, so you keep more of your gains.

Buffett made this recommendation more than 10 years ago, and over the last decade, the S&P 500, along with the index funds that track it, has gained more than 300%. If you had invested $10,000 in 2016, you'd have more than $40,000 today.

^SPX data by YCharts

Over time, that trend is likely to continue.

news.Title: Cathie Wood Continues to Buy the Dip on Crypto. Here Are 3 Crypto Investments That Need to Be on Your Radar.
news.Content:
Cathie Wood's Ark Invest has been studiously buying the dip with companies that touch crypto, gobbling up millions of dollars worth of Circle Internet Group (NYSE: CRCL), Coinbase Global (NASDAQ: COIN), and Robinhood Markets (NASDAQ: HOOD). As of Sept. 8, those three were weighted in Wood's ARK Innovation ETF (NYSEMKT: ARKK) at 6%, 4.6%, and 4.3%, respectively, of a $6.5 billion fund.

Because these three make up such a large share of her portfolio, investors should have them on their radar, even if they might not be the right kind of investment for them to buy right now.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

1. Circle is a bet on interest rates and stablecoins

Circle issues USDC , the second-largest stablecoin by market cap, with $74 billion in circulation.

Critically, USDC is backed by reserves of short-term Treasury bills and other interest-bearing cash equivalent assets. As the issuer, Circle captures the interest payments earned from those reserves. In Q2, its reserve income was $668 million, with an average reserve return of 3.5%.

That yield isn't something written in stone. The Federal Reserve's rate decisions determine short-term yields; cuts to the Fed's benchmark rate shrink Circle's reserve income, while hikes increase it.

Cathie Wood is buying the stock anyway. Her fund invested $16.3 million in Circle on March 24, even as it fell, with another purchase of $13.9 million in mid-July, and yet another $3.4 million invested on Aug. 31.

2. Coinbase is working to diversify

Today, Coinbase operates the largest U.S. crypto exchange, but it aspires to do more than connect investors to spot purchasing.

Its subscription and services revenue reached $555 million in the second quarter of this year, and 88% of its net revenue came from something other than Bitcoin spot trading. A big slice of its revenue now is interest payments on the USDC that's parked at Coinbase by its users. It also now has a platform for trading financial derivatives, like perpetual futures contracts , which could help boost its top line.

Ark Invest bought about $8 million of Coinbase shares on Aug. 2, right after a disappointing quarter sent the price lower, and then bought more again on Aug. 6. The company will not have the crypto market to itself, but its large user base and favorable positioning with regulators will make it a core part of the industry in the U.S. for the foreseeable future.

Story Continues

3. Robinhood now counts as a crypto investment

Robinhood is once again expanding into crypto with its launch of a new blockchain in July, though it's still a tertiary line of business for the company.

In Q2, the online brokerage platform reported record revenue of $1.3 billion, up 32% from a year prior, though its crypto revenue fell by 38% to $100 million. The transaction fees its new chain is bringing in could help its crypto segment grow a bit more. In August, users paid $6.6 million in chain fees for transacting on the network, up from $3.6 million the prior month.

But Robinhood has covered the transactions costs made in its own wallet since launch, and that 90-day subsidy expires Sept. 29. It remains to be seen how the chain performs once that subsidy ends; it could see a moderate drop in activity, reducing the fees it harvests.

Cathie Wood had cut Ark's stake in Robinhood in July 2026, then, on Sept. 3, she bought a bit more, perhaps as a result of the rapid success of the Robinhood Chain.

Assuming Robinhood can build out its blockchain with the lessons it learned from building its highly successful retail investing platform, the stock could do quite well from here.

news.Title: 【Follow法人】外資提款緯創逾3萬張！台積電也被賣48億元 反手狂掃力積電2.8萬張居冠
news.Content:
（下午4點38分更新買賣超個股）

台股今（10）日終場下跌242點，失守4萬7千點大關，外資也變臉終止連4買，反手賣超383.34億元，拖累三大法人合計賣超503.11億元。顧德投顧分析師黃紫東表示，受到美國CPI公布前觀望，以及部分資金可能轉往日本市場影響，外資目前較偏短線調節，只是「先休息一下」。觀察個股買賣超，外資今日提款緯創（3231）逾3.3萬張，台積電（2330）也被賣48億元，反手卻狂掃力積電（6770）逾2.8萬張居冠。

外資今日賣超前三大：緯創、群創、00406A

外資今日賣超以AI伺服器大廠緯創（3231）居冠，單日遭調節逾3.3萬張；面板股群創（3481）遭外資賣超逾3萬張排名第二；主動中信台灣收益（00406A）則遭賣超逾2.7萬張，位居第三。

其餘個股方面，二哥聯電（2303）也同步遭外資砍逾萬張；ETF方面，除了主動中信台灣收益遭賣超逾2.7萬張外，群益臺灣加權正2（00685L）也遭外資調節逾1.2萬張，今日外資賣超前十大共有2檔ETF入列。

值得注意的是台積電（2330）也遭外資賣超逾1,994張，若以今日收盤價估算，外資單日調節金額約48億元。

外資今日買超前三大：力積電、友達、凱基金

觀察外資今日買超個股，晶圓代工廠力積電（6770）以買超2.8萬張高居第一；面板股友達（2409）獲外資買超逾1.8萬張排名第二；凱基金（2883）則獲加碼逾1.3萬張，位居第三。

外資今日買盤明顯集中金融股，除了凱基金外，第一金（2892）、台中銀（2812）、兆豐金（2886）及臺企銀（2834）也進入前十大，前十大買超個股中共有5檔金融股。

值得注意的是，面板族群今日呈現不同調，外資一邊買超友達逾1.8萬張，另一邊則賣超群創逾3萬張。

外資轉賣383億元 黃紫東點出2大因素

黃紫東指出，外資今日轉為賣方主要有兩項因素，首先是市場等待美國CPI數據公布，在通膨及聯準會後續政策仍有不確定性的情況下，市場可能提前反應，因此外資先行降低股票部位、進行資金調節，屬於相對自然的現象。

另一項因素則是亞洲市場間的資金移動。黃紫東表示，新台幣近期雖然相對強勢，但日圓表現更為強勢，而外資進行資產配置時，通常會先決定資金進入哪個市場，再進一步選擇個股，因此部分資金可能暫時轉往日本市場，使外資在台股「先休息一下」。

黃紫東認為，目前還不到外資從大買直接轉為大賣的程度，比較像是「稍微轉個小彎」，先進行部分調節，若後續美國CPI數據不如市場預期，未來幾個交易日外資確實可能延續調節，不過仍須逐日觀察。

外資終止連四買 今回頭砍383億元

根據證交所公布籌碼動向，三大法人今日合計轉賣超503.11億元。其中，外資今日終止連4買，今日由買轉賣，回頭砍383.34億元。

投信則是延續買超，投信今日合計買超17.86億元，呈連2買。自營商則持續賣超137.62億元，其中自行買賣買超35.60億元，避險操作賣超102.02億元。

台股今日震盪走低，加權指數終場收在46,940點，下跌242點，失守4萬7千點關卡。成交金額約7,459億元；權王台積電（2330）終場收在2,450元，下跌15元。

news.Title: 挖到石油也沒用？緯創8月狂賺4,600億還掉價「廣達、鴻海無辜躺槍集體慘崩」分析師說溜嘴：這次與跟基本面無關
news.Content:
電子代工大廠緯創（3231）8月合併營收衝上4,600.65億元，月增49.26％、年增166.48％，不僅首度突破4,000億元大關，更創下歷史新高，這項「核爆級」的成長引發市場熱烈討論，網友紛紛驚嘆「這MoM（月增率）太扯了，根本是挖到石油吧」、「這營收根本是『緯屈』了，明天股價沒回200元說不過去吧？」然而，在基本面大好的利多加持下，緯創股價卻出現「利多不漲、震盪走低」的詭譎走勢，昨日（9月10日）收盤價下跌2.12％至185元，並引發「老AI族群」廣達、英業達等集體重挫。

壓制股價三大短線干擾因素

分析師指出，緯創呈現基本面大好、股價卻疲軟的現象，主要受到以下三大核心因素的短線干擾，一是GDR完成訂價，引發短線套利與比價賣壓，緯創公告海外存託憑證（GDR）完成訂價為58.88美元（折合普通股每股約186.24元），與當時普通股價格相比折價約5.5％。這導致市場出現強烈的「短線重新比價效應」與「GDR套利交易預期」，套利者賣出台股現股、認購折價的GDR，對短線股價造成沉重壓力。

二是發行新股稀釋股本的疑慮，緯創此次發行2,500萬單位GDR，相當於新增2.5億股普通股，股權稀釋比例約達7.29％。雖然募集到的14.72億美元，折合新台幣約465億元，將用於擴充美、越等地的AI伺服器產能與購料，長遠有利營運，惟股本膨脹在短線上會改變未來「每股盈餘（EPS）」的計算基礎，引發投資人擔憂而先逢高調整持股。

三是籌碼面外資調節與大盤轉弱雙重打擊，外資在GDR訂價後由買轉賣，單日就曾狂砍上萬張，例如9月8日外資大賣10,619張，籌碼面短線轉趨凌亂；此外，台股整體大盤走勢轉弱回檔，也加劇了市場順勢調節基本面利多的賣壓，形成「利多出盡」的短線格局。

法人看好中長線：AI伺服器動能無虞

雖然短線股價因籌碼與GDR比價效應受挫，但法人對緯創的中長期基本面仍極具信心，主要基於兩大理由，包括AI伺服器動能無虞，8月營收的高成長主要來自企業級AI伺服器機架出貨量較上月翻倍，且輝達新世代平台如VeraRubin、GB系列並未出現新舊迭代空窗期，高成長動能有望一路延續至第四季高峰。

且目標價與EPS獲上修，鑒於7、8月亮眼的營收表現，外資與本土投顧紛紛上修了第3季營收預期，並調升2026～2028年的EPS預估。目前FactSet調查的法人預估目標價中位數已看至277.5元。美銀投顧重申「買進」評等並將目標價調升至265元；凱基投顧更看好緯創2026年EPS有望翻倍挑戰17.65元，維持「增加持股」評等。

老AI受累重挫，廣達營收創高現支撐

受到緯創GDR利空外溢的拖累，廣達（2382）、英業達（2356）等AI代工族群集體重挫4％至7％，資深證券分析師指出，外資為了平衡在老AI族群間的權重持股，或者進行跨市場的套利鎖利，在砍緯創同時，連帶把廣達、鴻海（2317）等一併當作提款機大舉調節，這種下跌無關基本面衰退。

廣達8月營收同樣交出歷史新高達4239.71億元，分析師認為廣達營收動能依舊在AI代工中名列前茅，短線跌勢已有些過度反應，其關鍵支撐在321元，只要守穩，長線投資人不用盲目殺低。

短線籌碼利空，拉回視為布局良機

多數分析師認為，這波下跌是「短線籌碼利空疊加本益比修正」，長線基本面非但沒有轉弱，甚至出現「老AI拉回就是送分題」的樂觀中長線觀點，緯創技術面上只要守穩180至185元，即GDR訂價附近，短線利空出盡後，仍屬中長期的偏多整理格局，投資人可視為分批布局良機。

news.Title: Walmart Eyes CTV, AI and Self-Service Tools to Build a Bigger Ad Business
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Walmart Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

Walmart is scaling its advertising business through self-service buying tools, APIs, performance advertising and partnerships, aiming to serve advertisers ranging from small brands to major corporations.

Connected TV is a major growth priority: Walmart is using its VIZIO acquisition, onn TVs and partnerships with Magnite, Yahoo DSP, YouTube, Meta and TikTok to expand audience targeting and measurement across television and digital platforms.

Advertising offers a high-margin profit opportunity, with margins above 70% versus roughly 5% for core retail. Walmart is also investing in AI shopping tools such as Sparky, whose users and average order values have increased, while expanding into non-retail advertisers and international markets.

5 Defensive Stocks to Watch as CPI and the Fed Put the Rally to the Test

Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT) is expanding its advertising business beyond traditional retail media by building self-service tools, broadening its connected-TV capabilities and pursuing more advertising opportunities both inside and outside its shopping ecosystem, Walmart Connect U.S. General Manager Ryan Mayward said at the Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference.

Mayward, who became general manager about eight or nine months ago after initially joining Walmart Connect in sales, said the business has evolved during the past several years from a managed-service publisher model toward a scalable advertising platform. Earlier efforts centered on sponsorships tied to major shopping events and a nascent search business, he said. The company is now focused on performance advertising, self-service buying tools, application programming interfaces and partnerships with service providers.

Marketplace growth supports ad expansion

→ 3 Under-the-Radar Defense Stocks With Record Backlogs

Retail Earnings Just Exposed a Bigger Divide in the U.S. Consumer Economy

Mayward described Walmart's marketplace and advertising operations as "symbiotic." More third-party sellers can expand product assortment, attract customer attention and generate more gross merchandise value, while also increasing competition among sellers for consumer attention through advertising, particularly paid search.

Marketplace sellers compete through retail fundamentals such as price, shipping speed, product ratings, reviews and item-page content, but advertising provides another way to stand out, he said. Mayward added that a broader advertiser base can make advertising revenue more diversified and potentially less exposed to weakness in any one industry.

Story Continues

→ Ride-Share Reckoning: Tesla Drives Into Uber's Lane

Gold and Bitcoin Are Rebounding—2 ETFs Give Investors a Different Kind of Exposure

He said Walmart Connect is seeking to make its tools workable for advertisers of different sizes, from a small brand spending $1,000 per month to a large brand spending $10 million per month.

CTV strategy centers on VIZIO and external partners

Mayward said Walmart is particularly focused on connected television, including opportunities to make TV advertising more accessible to smaller and local businesses. The company completed its VIZIO acquisition on Aug. 4, according to Mayward, and sees the platform as a way to offer campaign setup, goal-based buying, automated optimization and measurement that are familiar to advertisers using search and social platforms.

→ High Gas Prices Aren't Budging—Here Are 3 Stocks That Benefit

Walmart has enabled Walmart audience targeting and measurement on VIZIO inventory, and 2026 is the first full year that Walmart Connect advertisers have been able to use the offering, Mayward said. He said adoption has been strong among large consumer packaged goods advertisers.

The company is also seeking to expand VIZIO's reach by selling more VIZIO televisions and placing the VIZIO smart-TV operating system on Walmart's onn private-label TVs. Mayward said the combined effort made the VIZIO operating system the leading smart-TV operating system in the U.S. during the first half of the year.

Walmart is working with Magnite to make Walmart Connect audience and measurement capabilities available on VIZIO inventory while allowing advertisers to buy through multiple demand-side platforms. Yahoo DSP advertisers can activate campaigns on the inventory, and Mayward said DV360 integration is expected to follow.

Separately, Walmart is in a beta phase with YouTube that allows advertisers to use Walmart data to target and measure campaigns on the video platform. Mayward said the initial managed-service approach is intended to help the companies develop a self-service campaign workflow. Walmart has also established advertising partnerships with Meta and TikTok.

AI shopping tools and measurement remain priorities

Mayward said Walmart is working with Google and OpenAI to enable discovery of Walmart products in their agentic shopping interfaces, though he characterized the activity as early and relatively small. Walmart is also investing in its own shopping agent, Sparky.

According to Mayward, Sparky's weekly active customers doubled year over year and rose 60% quarter over quarter. He said the average order value for Sparky shopping trips is 40% higher than for non-Sparky trips, citing use cases involving more considered purchases such as planning a tailgate party.

For advertisers, Walmart Connect is emphasizing measurement tied to business goals such as customer acquisition, household penetration, customer reactivation and larger shopping baskets. Mayward said the company measures online ads' impact on purchases in both the Walmart app and stores, and has introduced tools to measure sales lift and incrementality across display, video and search.

Walmart is also testing inventory- and price-aware end-of-aisle screens in certain stores. The screens can show sponsored messages intended to direct shoppers into relevant aisles, particularly in food and consumables, Mayward said.

Advertising viewed as incremental profit opportunity

Mayward said the company's advertising business has margins above 70%, compared with approximately 5% for Walmart's core retail business. He said Walmart views advertising profit as incremental rather than the result of shifting spending from other trade-investment categories.

While e-commerce growth and advertising growth are directly connected because more online shoppers and higher e-commerce GMV expand the advertising opportunity, Mayward said advertising can also grow beyond Walmart's e-commerce operations. This includes non-endemic advertisers such as insurance companies, financial-services firms, quick-service restaurants, entertainment companies and local businesses.

Walmart has begun offering non-endemic placements in its shopping app and through offsite advertising capabilities. Mayward said connected TV can further expand the company's addressable advertiser base.

Looking ahead, Walmart is working to place Sam's Club and international advertising operations on a common advertising technology stack. Mayward said the effort could improve use of data and advertising placements in those businesses while eventually supporting deeper relationships with global brands.

"We are building out the capabilities to be in all those places," Mayward said, referring to shopping environments, social platforms, television and short-form video. "As those capabilities mature, our advertising business opportunity size will be much bigger than that which is enabled by the retail business."

About Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT)

Walmart Inc is a multinational retail and technology company that operates supercenters, discount stores, neighborhood markets, e-commerce platforms and membership warehouse clubs. Its merchandise includes groceries, apparel, electronics, home goods, health and beauty products, general merchandise and other consumer products.

Founded by Sam Walton in 1962 and incorporated in 1969, Walmart is headquartered in Bentonville, Arkansas. The company serves customers through operations in the United States and international markets, including Mexico, Canada, China, India and several countries in Central America and Africa.

news.Title: Apple Event Rundown: What Was Announced?
news.Content:
The recent Apple AAPL event, which is the first major product event led by new CEO John Ternus, featured several hardware debuts, headlined by Apple's long-awaited entry into the foldable market. Here are a few key products that were announced:

The iPhone Duo: Apple officially unveiled its first-ever foldable smartphone. Built with a book-style hinge that opens to a large 7.6-inch inner display, it supports Apple Pencil and uses side-mounted Touch ID (skipping Face ID).

iPhone 18 Pro & Pro Max: Powered by the new 2nm A20 Pro chip and deeper Siri AI integrations, the Pro line introduces a groundbreaking 48MP Fusion Main camera with a physical variable aperture.

Apple Watch Series 12 & Ultra 4: The new watches focus heavily on health tech, introducing a more advanced health sensing system and an always-listening background microphone feature that can passively summarize conversational data throughout the day.

AirPods 5: The updated wireless earbuds bring improved durability, richer sound, and roughly 50% better active noise cancellation than their predecessors.

Apple's AAPL recent results reflected its strongest June quarter ever, with quarterly revenue of $109.4 billion growing 16% year-over-year. Adjusted EPS came in at $2.02, growing an even stronger 29% from the year-ago period.

Apple also reported double-digit revenue growth across iPhone, Mac, and Services, with similar gains in every geographic segment. Its installed base of active devices also reached an all-time high across its major product categories.

As usual, the iPhone remained the mega-cap tech giant's biggest revenue driver, with sales coming in at $54.3 billion and up 21.6% year over year.

news.Title: Goldman Sachs sends stark message to Tesla investors
news.Content:
Tesla just closed the book on one of the most anticipated product rollouts in company history, and Wall Street is still trying to figure out what it actually means for the stock.

The Cybercab is no longer a concept car on a stage. It is now picking up paying riders on real streets, and that changes the questions analysts are asking.

Goldman Sachs used the moment to lay out a detailed, somewhat cautious roadmap for how Tesla's robotaxi ambitions could translate into shareholder value, and the firm's answer is more nuanced than either the bulls or the bears wanted to hear.

Goldman resets Tesla on neutral rating with a very wide range

Goldman kept its rating on Tesla at Neutral, alongside a 12-month price target of $360, which sat below the stock's $376.37 closing price on Sept. 3. That gap signals that the bank sees limited near-term upside from current levels. Even as it acknowledges Tesla's long-term autonomy story.

What stands out is the width of Goldman's outcome range. The firm's bull case points to roughly $500 a share. Other more bearish analyst scenarios have put the stock as low as around $150, according to Investing.com . That spread underscores how much of Tesla's valuation now hinges on execution rather than the primary auto business.

More Tesla:

Tesla sales rebound hides costly problem for investors

Tesla record revenue masks cash burn, $1B SpaceX swing

Elon Musk, Tesla and SpaceX face serious questions from investors

On the downside, Goldman flagged slower electric vehicle demand, intensifying competition, tariff pressure, delays to Full Self-Driving and other product timelines. The general margin strains, as the factors are most likely to drag the stock toward its lower bound.

Those are largely familiar risks, but the note ties them directly to the robotaxi thesis rather than treating them separately.

The upside case leans heavily on faster EV adoption, earlier product launches, and a bigger-than-expected financial contribution from AI-driven products including FSD, Optimus, and robotaxis.

Goldman's $360 target also landed below other major Wall Street firms such as JPMorgan, which held a Neutral rating with a $445 target, and Morgan Stanley, which kept an Equal-weight rating with a $400 target.

Cybercab's cost edge, by the numbers

The centerpiece of Goldman's argument is cost. Tesla began offering robotaxi rides in the Cybercab following its Sept. 3 event in Austin and said its Robotaxi fleet had surpassed 1 million miles driven without human supervision.

That milestone gave Goldman a growing pool of real-world operating data to incorporate alongside its projections.

Story Continues

If Tesla can hit its targeted Cybercab cost price of $20,000 to $30,000 at scale, Goldman estimated that the vehicle could carry a per-mile cost advantage of roughly five to 30 cents. That is compared with rival autonomous vehicles priced between $50,000 and $100,000, GuruFocus reported . That gap is meaningful in a business where margins are won or lost on cents per mile.

Goldman credited that potential edge to Tesla's unboxed manufacturing approach and its camera-only sensor system, which avoids the lidar and radar hardware that adds cost to many competing platforms. It is the same low-cost philosophy Tesla has applied to its consumer vehicles, now extended to a purpose-built robotaxi.

The note was not purely promotional. Goldman also estimated that Tesla's fully driverless operations experienced an accident, regardless of fault, roughly every 50,000 to 70,000 miles, based on NHTSA crash data through mid-July combined with Tesla's own disclosures for Austin, Dallas and Houston, according to Investing.com .

That figure gives investors a concrete safety benchmark to track as the fleet scales.

Software, not hardware, will decide the business case

Despite the cost advantage, Goldman was clear that a cheap vehicle alone will not make or break Tesla's robotaxi economics.

The bigger swing factor is whether Tesla can expand its autonomous driving software across more markets, which would raise vehicle utilization and let software margins carry more of the business.

A wider operating footprint would let Tesla spread its vehicle cost base across more miles while generating additional revenue, and making software a potentially larger driver of Robotaxi increasingly central to profitability rather than the hardware itself. That is a subtle but important shift in how Goldman frames the investment case.

The bank pointed to Tesla's own safety data as early evidence that the software is improving. In North America, vehicles running FSD Supervised on Tesla's fourth-generation hardware recorded roughly 75% to 85% fewer automatic emergency braking events and 40% to 90% fewer minor and major collisions compared with vehicles not using FSD, as reported by Investing.com .

Tesla is still playing catch-up on scale. Waymo had about 988 autonomous vehicles registered in Texas alone, compared with 45 Cybercabs for Tesla at launch.

That gap helps illustrate why Goldman keeps emphasizing the software performance and network argument rather than declaring victory on cost alone.

What it means for Tesla investors

The market's initial reaction was not celebratory. Tesla shares fell about 6% after the Cybercab event, with the launch drawing criticism for its limited specifics.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration opened an audit query covering roughly 1,000 Cybercabs to examine Tesla's compliance with the federal safety standards.

That regulatory scrutiny is important for investors because it adds a variable Goldman's cost model cannot fully price in. A vehicle built without a steering wheel or pedals faces standards written for human-driven cars, and the outcome of the audit could affect the pace of Tesla's broader Cybercab deployment.

For shareholders, the takeaway from Goldman's note is less about a single price target and more about what to watch next.

Cost advantages are real but secondary. So investors weighing Tesla stock may get more signal from fleet expansion, software performance data and regulatory outcomes than from any one event headline in the months ahead.

news.Title: HIVE joins Google, Microsoft, and Amazon in new Canada data center pledge
news.Content:
BUZZ HPC , a sovereign AI cloud and high-performance computing (HPC) provider and a wholly owned subsidiary of HIVE Digital Technologies (Nasdaq: HIVE), signed Canada's Responsible Data Centre Development Principles on Sep. 8, joining a list of signatories that includes Google, Microsoft, Amazon Web Services, Meta, Anthropic, and OpenAI.

The principles, published by Canada's federal government on Sep. 3, set a national framework for how data centers should be built and operated across the country.

Data centers are large facilities filled with servers that store, process and move the digital information behind everything from banking and healthcare to artificial intelligence. As demand for AI infrastructure grows, so does the strain these facilities place on local electricity grids, water supplies and communities.

Related: GameStop's record quarter came with a $75 million Bitcoin loss

Five commitments, one standard

The framework lays out five core principles. Data centers must create lasting local benefits including jobs, training and tax contributions. They must not shift electricity costs onto Canadian households or existing businesses. They must minimize freshwater use and environmental impact.

They must be transparent about local effects on power, water, noise and emissions. And they must deliver strategic value to Canada through investment, supply chain participation and digital resilience.

Craig Tavares, President and COO of BUZZ HPC, said the company views the principles as a foundation for building an industry critical to Canada's competitiveness.

"Canada does not have to choose between building the digital infrastructure our economy needs and building it responsibly," Tavares said in the government's published signatory list.

The only crypto-linked name on the list

HIVE Digital Technologies, its parent company, operates Bitcoin mining and data center facilities across Canada, Sweden and Paraguay.

The signing comes weeks after BUZZ HPC announced a $350 million, five-year AI cloud services deal powered by NVIDIA GPUs at its facility in Merritt, British Columbia.
